hero.subheadline: I turn game mechanics into 30-second experiences that move IPM and ROAS — then build the AI workflows and web systems that let a team ship them at scale.

about.statement: I came to ads from making real games — so I know what makes a mechanic sticky. Today I build playables, lead the creative behind them, and design the AI workflows that let one person do the work of a team.

projects.title: Bus Away
projects.summary: Tap the cars in the right order to fill each bus before the queue piles up. A clean traffic-jam puzzle that teaches itself in the first tap.

projects.title: Water Sort
projects.summary: The classic water-sort loop with a twist: a frozen column that cracks as you sort. Two guided moves, then the player is on their own.

projects.title: Hungry Gecko
projects.summary: Feed numbered color blocks to the gecko and watch a pixel-art picture come alive. Satisfying stacking with a reveal at every step.

projects.title: Wool Block Jam
projects.summary: Swipe knitted wool blocks out through the matching colored gates. Cozy, tactile textures on a quick-to-read jam puzzle.

projects.title: Bead Fill Color Block
projects.summary: Slide coloured blocks into the board and fill a pixel-bead Pharaoh before you run out of moves. A sliding-block puzzle with a tight 15-move hook.

projects.title: Jigsaw Solitaire
projects.summary: Swap scrambled cards to rebuild a famous painting. A calm jigsaw-meets-solitaire puzzle with art-gallery visuals.

projects.title: Worm Color Blast
projects.summary: Guide cute color worms to their holes and blast away the chocolate wall above. Path-finding puzzle that reads even at thumbnail size.

projects.title: Tricky Prank
projects.summary: Help the poor lady out of a messy situation by picking the right item. A short story-driven brain teaser with a funny payoff.

projects.title: Brainrot Merge
projects.summary: Drop and merge meme characters inside a jar until they evolve into bigger ones. Physics-based merge with trending Brainrot faces.

projects.title: Sprunkie Music Box
projects.summary: Drag outfits onto Sprunkie characters to build a beat, one layer at a time. A creative music-mixing playable with a horror twist.

experience.intro: Two years deep in-house, years of freelance across very different products, and my own ventures on the side. I like learning by shipping — so the map keeps growing.

branches.label: In-house
branches.title: JOYBIT · Brave Holdings
branches.body: I was JOYBIT's first playable ads developer — part of Brave Holdings, one of Vietnam's largest mobile game groups. I set up playable production from zero: the workflow, the network-ready build process and the quality bar every playable after was held to. Starting from scratch never meant starting small. Those playables stood next to the big studios' work and outperformed it — and they gave JOYBIT the confidence to step into mobile puzzle, one of the toughest genres on the store.
branches.highlight: First playable hire. I built the pipeline the studio still ships on.

branches.label: Freelance
branches.title: Outsource for studios & businesses
branches.body: Playables for studios and agencies — and beyond ads: a B2B enterprise platform covering CRM, operations and HR for a manufacturing company. I still take outside projects today.

branches.label: AI workflows
branches.title: AI-native production
branches.body: I build the AI framework my team works in: reusable skills, automated creative workflows and a manager–worker setup across models — so I can run several projects at once and customise assets and mechanics fast.

branches.label: Own ventures
branches.title: Startup, community & indie games
branches.meta: Products I own end to end
branches.body: Creative Dash Lab, my startup for UA teams. Tatadex, a game community site with over a million page views a month. And Metal Sail, my indie studio: award-winning jam games, and now web games live on CrazyGames and Playgama.

ai.intro: I don't just use AI — I build the system my team works in. One brief goes in; an orchestrator splits it into tasks, hands them to specialised workers, and checks the results before anything ships.

steps.name: Orchestrator
steps.detail: Plans, splits and reviews the work

steps.name: Workers
steps.detail: Parallel tasks through a custom CLI over model APIs

steps.name: Skills & workflows
steps.detail: Reusable recipes for assets, mechanics, localisation, export

steps.name: Ship
steps.detail: Playable variants ready for every network

points: A working framework for the team: shared skills, rules and automated workflows for creative playables
Vibe-coding in production — real projects that make money, not demos
Manager–worker setup across Claude, Codex and a custom CLI over many model APIs
Lets me multitask and stay flexible with custom assets and mechanics

ventures.title: Creative Dash Lab
ventures.body: A platform for UA teams to produce playable ads and video faster: a drag-and-drop Playable Canvas with bulk variants, one-click conversion between ad networks, asset extract-and-replace, and video resizing — all in the browser.

ventures.title: Enterprise operations platform
ventures.body: An all-in-one system for a manufacturing company: CRM with a stage-based pipeline, partners, products with versioned pricing, contracts and orders, purchasing, finance, tasks by department, an internal wiki and role-based access. Client identity is removed here.

ventures.title: Tatadex
ventures.body: The go-to guide for the mobile game Clash of Critters: campaign line-ups, tier lists, boss guides and a card-trading board, in three languages.

webGames.title: Gangster Life: Neon Shores
webGames.blurb: Steal cars, outrun five-star police chases and take back the family diner on a neon beach coast — a full open city running in the browser.
